C: keep today's behaviour and only correct the HELD alert text to say the prices shipped. Cheapest; the leak stays.

evidence: bacon | Fareway | 'Fareway Hickory Smoked Bacon 2.5 lb (only $3.99/lb)' | price_text $9.97 | size 2.5 lb | unit_price 1.596 | basis 'size 2.5 lb (per-lb marker was in the NAME only)' (candidates-2026-09-29). $9.97 / 2.5 lb = $3.988/lb; 1.596 = 3.99 / 2.5.

Get-ItemPrice (pricing-math-lib.ps1 line 304) prices from priceText + ' ' + nameText, so it took the NAME's '$3.99' rate as the item price; the NAME-only per-lb branch (lines 862-877) then divided that rate by the 2.5 lb size again.

The same wrong value was PUBLISHED on 2026-09-28 (guards wow line: 'the old cheapest was a sale row (Fareway ... (only $3.99/lb))' at $1.60); today flag-verification caught it and apply-cell-quarantine WITHHELD the cell (08:15:20). Quarantine worked as designed.
Fareway carries a correctly priced twin row of the same bacon: 'Fareway Hickory Smoked Bacon' $9.97 / 2.5 lb = 3.988 sale.

surface_fix.what: the NAME-only per-lb branch must not divide a per_item that is already the name's stated $X/lb rate
surface_fix.exact_change: in the unit -eq 'lb' / kind.perlb block (lines 862-877): when the NAME carries an explicit money-per-lb rate ('$ N / lb'), return per_item as the per-lb rate (basis 'per-lb rate stated in the name') instead of per_item / size

items.root_cause: one reader, two texts: Get-ItemPrice reads price and name as one string, so a Fareway ad line that prints its own per-lb rate in the name ('(only $3.99/lb)') has that rate taken as the item price, and a later branch that assumes per_item is a package price divides it again. Measured class on candidates-2026-09-29: 6 distinct rows (all Fareway) carry a money token in the name that differs from price_text; 5 are multibuy '(N/$X)' lines whose price_text already equals the per-item price, 1 is the per-lb rate that misprices.

root_fix.what: the item price comes from price_text whenever price_text holds a money token; the name is read for a price only when price_text has none
root_fix.exact_change: Get-ItemPrice: parse priceText first; fall back to priceText + nameText only when priceText carries no money token. Keep the concatenated string for the KIND flags (perlb, multibuy markers) later branches read. Before landing: rebuild the board in a scratch clone and diff every cell's per_unit against comparison-2026-09-29; expected moves = 1 (bacon/Fareway). Any other move stops the item.

prevention.what: the engine's ad-line price reader, the producer of the per-unit: an item price never comes from the product NAME when the price field has one (b61b08 was the same two-readers shape on a Hy-Vee Perks line)
prevention.exact_change: as root_fix, plus a compare-deals -SelfTest arithmetic case built from the frozen Fareway bacon row
